name: PTR Classification
description: Classify PTR hostnames and add matching ptrclassify taxonomy tags to the queried MISP attribute.
requirements: ptrclassify >=0.3.0,<0.4.0 and dnspython, included in the minimal and all installation extras
A DNS resolver that supports PTR queries for IP lookups
Enable the ptrclassify taxonomy in MISP to manage the returned tags; no API key or ptrclassify service is required
Install the ptrclassify MISP object template. A matching template is bundled in misp-modules for PyMISP releases that do not yet ship it.
features: Resolve IPv4 and IPv6 addresses and classify every distinct PTR hostname with the local ptrclassify library.
Preserve the queried address in the classifier's PTR record so IPv4-encoded hostnames return the ip-encoded naming tag and embedded_ip hint.
Classify hostname and domain values directly without a DNS lookup. Address-dependent hints are only available for IP inputs.
Preserve the input attribute UUID, existing tags, comment and detection flag while adding matching taxonomy tags.
Hover displays the enrichment. Importing expansion results applies the returned tags in MISP.
PTR names are operator-controlled. Classification and location hints are heuristic and are not verified usage or geolocation.

For IP lookups, return one dns-record object containing the reverse-DNS owner in queried-domain and all distinct PTR targets in ptr-record. Tag each PTR answer with its own classification and add the union of tags to the queried attribute.
Return one ptrclassify object per hostname, with repeated classification, category, label, confidence, evidence and rule-id fields instead of standalone summary text.
Classification fields use the corresponding machine tag as their attribute comment to preserve associations. Location fields use a rule-ID/code comment to identify each candidate.
Return structured location-code, location-city, location-region, location-country, location-confidence, location-evidence, location-rule-id and location-description fields when present.
Preserve embedded-ip, cloud-region and conflict hints as object attributes. Record the classifier-version and whether any label matched.

Each ptrclassify object characterizes the queried attribute and is derived-from the DNS object for IP lookups. The DNS object references the original attribute with related-to. Direct hostname/domain classification does not invent a DNS observation.

input.domain_ip: For domain|ip, the IP component is queried; the original composite attribute is retained.

output.response: results.Attribute contains only the original queried attribute with matching tags. results.Object contains one ptrclassify object per hostname and, for IP inputs, one dns-record object for the observed PTR answer set.
output.tags: Matching machine tags, such as ptrclassify:access="mobile", are returned in each attribute's Tag list. The input attribute retains its original UUID so MISP can associate the tags with the queried attribute.
output.new_attributes: All newly generated object attributes use to_ids=false. The queried attribute retains its detection flag.
output.no_match: Return the input, a ptrclassify object with matched=0, and any observed DNS object without adding taxonomy tags. Existing tags and any potential location hints are preserved.
output.errors: Missing PTR records, resolver failures, timeouts and invalid inputs return an error without tagged results.
output.dns_template: Use the existing dns-record template: queried-domain holds the in-addr.arpa or ip6.arpa owner, and ptr-record holds domain-typed PTR targets. No forward A/AAAA records are inferred.

nameserver.description: Optional DNS server for IP lookups. Hostname and domain inputs do not query DNS. Resolver timeout is two seconds and the total lookup lifetime is five seconds.

examples.description: Classify a supplied PTR-style hostname locally, in either hover or expansion mode.

Classify an IPv4 PTR answer while retaining address context. Return one ptrclassify object and one dns-record object. Tags are added to the IP and the ptr-record attribute. Expected results depend on the current DNS answer.
